claims.text: Sucralfate: caution in chronic renal failure or dialysis: absorbed aluminum isn't excreted, and accumulation/toxicity (osteodystrophy, osteomalacia, encephalopathy) has occurred.
claims.quote: Patients with chronic renal failure or those receiving dialysis have impaired excretion of absorbed aluminum. In addition, aluminum does not cross dialysis membranes because it is bound to albumin and transferrin plasma proteins. Aluminum accumulation and toxicity (aluminum osteodystrophy, osteomalacia, encephalopathy) have been described in patients with renal impairment. Sucralfate should be used with caution in patients with chronic renal failure.
claims.locator: Warnings and Precautions › Chronic Renal Failure and Dialysis

claims.text: Aluminum-containing antacids may add to the aluminum load.
claims.quote: Concomitant use of sucralfate with other products that contain aluminum, such as aluminum-containing antacids, may increase the total body burden of aluminum.
claims.locator: Warnings and Precautions › Chronic Renal Failure and Dialysis

claims.text: the risk rises with advancing gestational age and with prior uterine surgery, including cesarean delivery.
